page: Microsoft Azure F80ads_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Fadsv7 family. It features 80 dedicated physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 320.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage consists of a 9449 GB NVMe SSD, and the server is premium storage capable. It operates under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the F80ads_v7 demonstrates top-tier performance, placing in the top 10% for both single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests. Its memory subsystem achieves top-tier read-only small block bandwidth of 14260.32 GB/sec and large block write bandwidth of 213.34 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression capabilities are also in the top 10%, with a PassMark CPU encryption score of 117725.96 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 1012.5 GB/sec. Database operations are highly efficient, as shown by a Redis SET throughput of 202.34 million operations per second.

For machine learning workloads, the server achieves top-tier prompt processing speeds of 5722.82 tokens per second on a small 135M model, though text generation for the same model drops to an average tier of 231.82 tokens per second. Medium 7B model text generation remains in the top 10% at 54.82 tokens per second, while large 70B model prompt processing falls to the middle 50% tier at 23.62 tokens per second. This indicates a performance tradeoff where prompt processing scales well on smaller models but text generation and larger model processing are relatively constrained by the lack of dedicated GPU hardware.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F80ads_v7 offers a high density of dedicated physical cores and substantial local NVMe storage, making it a viable alternative to GPU-accelerated instances for CPU-bound tasks. The server is suited for high-throughput database operations, static web serving, data compression pipelines, and CPU-based language model inference.
